Extract or replace regex matches, in parallel

Source: R/par-extract.R
par_extract.Rd

  • par_extract() returns the first match in each string, like regmatches(x, regexpr(pattern, x)), but with NA where nothing matches.

  • par_extract_all() returns every match, like regmatches(x, gregexpr(pattern, x)).

  • par_locate() finds where the first match is, like regexpr(pattern, x).

  • par_locate_all() finds where every match is, like gregexpr(pattern, x).

  • par_replace() replaces the first match, like sub(pattern, replacement, x).

  • par_replace_all() replaces every match, like gsub(pattern, replacement, x).

All use the syntax of Rust's regex crate, as par_detect() does.

Usage

par_extract(
  x,
  pattern,
  group = 0L,
  fixed = FALSE,
  nthreads = getOption("parvenu.threads", 0L)
)

par_extract_all(
  x,
  pattern,
  group = 0L,
  fixed = FALSE,
  nthreads = getOption("parvenu.threads", 0L)
)

par_locate(
  x,
  pattern,
  group = 0L,
  fixed = FALSE,
  nthreads = getOption("parvenu.threads", 0L)
)

par_locate_all(
  x,
  pattern,
  group = 0L,
  fixed = FALSE,
  nthreads = getOption("parvenu.threads", 0L)
)

par_replace(
  x,
  pattern,
  replacement,
  fixed = FALSE,
  nthreads = getOption("parvenu.threads", 0L)
)

par_replace_all(
  x,
  pattern,
  replacement,
  fixed = FALSE,
  nthreads = getOption("parvenu.threads", 0L)
)

Arguments

x

A string vector, or an object convertible by as.character().

pattern

The regex, or the literal string to find if fixed = TRUE: one string, or one per string of x, as in stringi::stri_detect_regex(). Each distinct pattern is compiled once.

group

The capture group to extract: 0 for the whole match, 1 for the first group, and so on. par_extract() also takes several, such as 0:3. It then returns a matrix with a column per group, from one search.

fixed

If TRUE, pattern is found as it is, as in grepl(fixed = TRUE): no character has a special meaning.

nthreads

A whole number: the max number of threads to use. 0 means the RAYON_NUM_THREADS environment variable, or else all cores. The default is the parvenu.threads option, or 0 if that isn't set. Inputs too small to keep that many threads busy get fewer, and more threads than cores count as all cores.

replacement

The string to put in place of each match. Unless fixed = TRUE, $1 stands for the first capture group, ${name} for a named one, and $$ for a $. Write ${1}a, not $1a, which means a group named 1a. R's \\1 is not a group here.

Value

  • par_extract(), par_replace(), and par_replace_all(): a string vector as long as x, with the names of x, as regmatches(), sub(), and gsub() keep them. NA where x or pattern is NA. For par_extract(), also NA where nothing matches or the group took no part in the match. With several groups, par_extract() returns a string matrix instead, with a row per string (named as x is) and a column per group, as stringi::stri_match_first_regex() does.

  • par_extract_all(): a list as long as x. Each element is a string vector of the matches, character(0) if none, or NA where x or pattern is NA. It finds the matches that par_count() counts. For a group, it has NA where the group took no part in a match.

  • par_locate(): an integer matrix with a row per string and columns start and end, positions of characters, as in stringi::stri_locate_first_regex(). An empty match has end one less than start. NA where there is no match, or the group took no part in it.

  • par_locate_all(): a list as long as x. Each element is such a matrix with a row per match, no rows if none, or one row of NA where x or pattern is NA.

Details

par_extract() can return a capture group instead of the whole match, which takes the place of lookaround. It can also return several groups at once, as a matrix.

The threads find the matches and build the replaced strings. Only R's thread may turn them into R strings, so that part runs serially. Strings that par_replace() and par_replace_all() leave unchanged are not copied.

Examples

x <- c("born 1999 in Oslo", "no year", NA)
par_extract(x, "[0-9]{4}")
#> [1] "1999" NA     NA    
par_extract(x, "born ([0-9]+)", group = 1)
#> [1] "1999" NA     NA    
par_extract(x, "born ([0-9]+) in (\\w+)", group = 1:2)
#>      [,1]   [,2]  
#> [1,] "1999" "Oslo"
#> [2,] NA     NA    
#> [3,] NA     NA    
par_extract_all(c("#rstats and #rust", "none", NA), "#(\\w+)", group = 1)
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "rstats" "rust"  
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> character(0)
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> [1] NA
#> 
par_locate(x, "[0-9]{4}")
#>      start end
#> [1,]     6   9
#> [2,]    NA  NA
#> [3,]    NA  NA
par_locate_all(x, "[a-z]+")
#> [[1]]
#>      start end
#> [1,]     1   4
#> [2,]    11  12
#> [3,]    15  17
#> 
#> [[2]]
#>      start end
#> [1,]     1   2
#> [2,]     4   7
#> 
#> [[3]]
#>      start end
#> [1,]    NA  NA
#> 
par_replace(x, "[0-9]", "#")
#> [1] "born #999 in Oslo" "no year"           NA                 
par_replace_all(x, "[0-9]", "#")
#> [1] "born #### in Oslo" "no year"           NA                 
par_replace_all("Smith, John", "(\\w+), (\\w+)", "$2 $1")
#> [1] "John Smith"
